vocabulary.meaning_en: the start of a new year (January 1st)
vocabulary.example: It will be a new year soon.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a firm decision to do something
vocabulary.note_ar: New Year's resolution = قرار للسنة الجديدة
vocabulary.note_en: "New Year's resolution" = a goal for the new year.
vocabulary.example: Have you made any New Year's resolutions?
At the beginning of the year, decide on a goal.

vocabulary.meaning_en: choose to do something after thinking
vocabulary.example: You should decide to do something.
I'm planning to go to the gym every day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: decide what you want to achieve
vocabulary.example: Let's set a goal for this year.
I want to achieve my goals.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a running race of about 42 km
vocabulary.example: I'm going to run a marathon.
I'm looking forward to the challenge.
A new year brings new hope.

vocabulary.meaning_en: keep your body healthy and strong
vocabulary.example: I will try to stay fit and well.
I'm hoping to give up caffeine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the thing in coffee and tea that keeps you awake
vocabulary.example: Coffee has a lot of caffeine.

fine_lines.title: goal vs resolution
fine_lines.explanation_ar: goal = هدف تريد تحقيقه. resolution = قرار حازم، وغالبًا في بداية السنة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A "goal" is something you want to achieve. A "resolution" is a firm decision, often at New Year.

examples.sentence: My goal is to read 20 books.
My New Year's resolution is to exercise more.

fine_lines.title: going to vs hoping to
fine_lines.explanation_ar: I'm going to = خطة مؤكدة. I'm hoping to = أتمنى، ليس مؤكدًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "I'm going to" = a sure plan. "I'm hoping to" = a wish, not sure.

examples.sentence: I'm going to run a marathon.
I'm hoping to learn more English.

expressions.phrase: Have you made any New Year's resolutions?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل وضعت أي قرارات للسنة الجديدة؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asking about plans for the new year.
expressions.example: Have you made any plans for the holiday?
My goal is to read more. What's yours?
Sorry I'm late. The bus was slow.
Hi! What are you talking about?

expressions.phrase: I can't believe tomorrow is the first day of the New Year!
expressions.meaning_ar: لا أصدق أن الغد هو أول يوم في السنة الجديدة!
expressions.example: I can't believe it's Friday already!

expressions.phrase: The year went by so fast.
expressions.example: This week went by so fast.

expressions.phrase: I'm planning to go to the gym every day.
expressions.meaning_ar: أخطط للذهاب إلى الصالة الرياضية كل يوم.
expressions.example: I'm planning to visit my grandparents.

expressions.phrase: I'm looking forward to the challenge.
expressions.example: The exam is hard, but I'm looking forward to the challenge.

expressions.phrase: I'm hoping to learn more English.
expressions.meaning_ar: أتمنى أن أتعلم مزيدًا من الإنجليزية.
expressions.example: I'm hoping to find a new job.

expressions.phrase: I will try to stay fit and well.
expressions.meaning_ar: سأحاول أن أحافظ على لياقتي وصحتي.
expressions.example: This year I will try to sleep early.

grammar.title: Talking about the future: going to / planning to / hoping to / will try to
grammar.explanation_ar: للخطط المستقبلية: I'm going to + فعل (خطة)، I'm planning to + فعل، I'm hoping to + فعل (أمنية)، I will try to + فعل (محاولة).
grammar.explanation_en: Future plans: "going to" (plan), "planning to", "hoping to" (wish), "will try to" (effort).
examples: I'm going to run a marathon.
I'm planning to go to the gym.
I'm hoping to learn more English.

grammar.title: Present perfect questions: Have you made ...?
grammar.explanation_ar: نسأل عن شيء فعلته حتى الآن: Have you + التصريف الثالث؟ ومع yet في السؤال: Have you made a resolution yet?
grammar.explanation_en: Ask about something done up to now: "Have you + past participle?" Add "yet" in questions.
examples: Have you made a resolution yet?

questions.question: A firm decision for the new year is a New Year's ...
I'm ____ to learn more English. (a wish, not sure)
"I'm hoping to give up caffeine." Give up means ...
